messages:
emma: Quick q — onboarding hedgehog-6b. Found the license (link below) that has a 'no commercial redistribution of modified weights' clause and an attribution requirement. We're planning quantized derivatives for Dedicated + Private; is that a hard block? cc @maggie-legal @raj

raj: I skimmed it earlier. If it's 'no commercial redistribution' that usually means we can't hand out quantized weights to paying customers. Serving via our API is probably OK. Need the exact text to be sure.

luis: FWIW, our Dedicated sales sometimes expect a model bundle or a preloaded image. If we ship a .pt/.bin that's redistribution. Private (VPC) hosting w/o exporting is different.

emma: Plan we had: 1) run quant experiments, 2) upload quantized model to internal S3 for serving, 3) optionally include downloadable artifact for Dedicated installs. Should we stop step 3 immediately?

maggie-legal: Short answer: probably yes for redistribution to paying customers. Please paste the exact license link + the clause. Also include how you plan to attribute (UI text/docs) so we can confirm compliance. I'll open a ticket for a formal opinion.

emma: License: https://example.org/hedgehog-6b/license.txt
Clause excerpt:
"You may not redistribute modified model weights for commercial purposes. Attribution 'Hedgehog-6B (OpenHedge) - Model authors: HedgeLabs' required in product docs."

maggie-legal: That wording suggests: serving the model via our hosted API is allowed; distributing the binaries (quantized or not) to customers for commercial use is likely prohibited. For Dedicated, handing over the weight files as part of the install would be redistribution. I'll escalate.

legal-bot: Created ticket RH-1967: "Hedgehog-6B licensing: redistribution of quantized weights for Dedicated sales" — assignee: @maggie-legal. ETA ~2 business days.

raj: Potential technical workaround: avoid shipping binaries. Offer an "on-demand quantize" step run inside customer infra (or as a post-provisioning job) so final weights are produced within customer environment and never leave it. That could sidestep redistribution.

luis: That's doable — we can bake a quantization job into the Dedicated installer that runs once. Need to confirm installer permissions + we should produce a signed audit log. Also hits product timelines.

emma: OK I'll pause packaging/export steps and stop sharing any quantized artifacts externally. I'll update onboarding doc & the eval runbook to emphasize host-only evals until legal clears. Will drop a short note in the sales pre-sale checklist too so folks don't promise downloads.

maggie-legal: Thanks. Please add a redlined example of what "deliverable" would look like to RH-1967 (e.g., full weights tarball vs. container with weights baked in vs. quant pipeline only). cc: @sales when you add the note. :thumbsup:

emma: Will do. Thanks all.
